paragraph_audit.reason: The existing anchors capture the patent Use and sale grants, their limited claim scope, and termination on filing qualifying patent litigation. The patent grant also expressly covers making, having made, offering to sell, importing, and otherwise transferring the Work (lines 76–81). These actions cannot all be faithfully represented by the available activities; the unmatched actions are making, having made, offering to sell, importing, and otherwise transferring.

Section 5 creates a default rule for the distinct action of intentionally submitting a Contribution for inclusion: absent an explicit contrary statement, it is under this License without additional terms. It preserves the terms of any separate executed license agreement regarding those Contributions. Submit is not an available activity, so this operative submission rule and its exception cannot be faithfully represented.

coverage_notes: Apache License 2.0 section 3's patent grant includes making, having made, offering to sell, selling, importing, and otherwise transferring the Work. Existing anchors represent Use and selling; the remaining enumerated actions cannot be modeled with the available activities. Section 5's operative rule concerns intentionally submitting a Contribution, an action not available in the activity set. No clauses were added because neither gap can be faithfully expressed without inventing a different action.
